subject: Muse-inspired white-and-charcoal panda with a small green dragon on its anatomical right shoulder (world -X, viewer-left), authored as a complete articulated 3D toy.
style: Soft, compact storybook panda with actual short geometric fur, expressive inset features and a detailed green dragon; browser PBR edition
prompt: Re-author the Muse-inspired panda as a compact, expressive, complete animated 3D character. Use the supplied Muse portrait for proportions, black-and-ivory palette, warm brown eyes, broad cheeks, soft muzzle, smile and the small green dragon on its anatomical right/viewer-left shoulder. Replace stacked joint balls with continuous weighted arms and legs. Model visible short fur, eyelids, layered glossy eyes, nostrils, mouth crease, ears, paws, toes and a rear tail. The shoulder dragon must have shaped head/body, eyes, nostrils, smile, horns, frills, scaled green skin, segmented belly, claws, curved tail and complete scalloped wings with raised spars. Include all these features in the skinned GLB, not only in the render. Use embedded procedural fur/scale surface textures and opaque physically based materials. Preserve a small golden crafting orb as an explicitly authored action prop. Idle breathes and the dragon nods; making_something rubs and rolls the orb between the paws; working lifts it for inspection; milestone_level_up presents it with a happy arm lift. Author all unseen surfaces, rig, fur placement and motion; do not claim recovered geometry, hair simulation, facial capture, Weft compatibility or exact Muse-quality equivalence.
authored_assumptions: The supplied opaque 2D portrait supplies appearance only; back, underside, rig, topology, UVs, weights and fur placement are newly authored.
Fur is a bounded short triangular-blade groom plus embedded surface textures, not a physically simulated or film-density hair system.
Arms and legs have continuous meshes with blended two-bone skinning. Torso, head, paws and facial components remain separate authored surfaces.
Eyes, eyelids, nose, mouth and paw digits are modeled geometry, not independently actuated facial muscles or fingers.
The green dragon stays attached to the torso-side anatomical-right shoulder helper; head, tail and wings have local authored controls only.
The golden orb is an authored action prop, not part of the reference portrait. Crafting gestures do not change its geometry or simulate manufacture.
General PBR edition: embedded normal maps, short fur and glossy surfaces have not been reduced to or approved by the Weft diffuse-only profile.
All native glTF transforms are authored meters/Y-up/+Z-front after Blender export; scale is not calibrated to the live simulator.
The neutral pose is arms resting beside the rounded body, feet flat, face forward; it is not an observed simulator pose.

source_prompt: Create a complete editable matte 3D interpretation of the user-supplied Muse panda reference: white face and belly, charcoal eye patches, ears, limbs and small tail, and a small green dragon on the anatomical right shoulder/world -X/viewer-left. Preserve that side and palette. Author unseen surfaces and a controllable toy rig explicitly. Include independently weighted upper arms, forearms, thighs and shins on both sides, with visible rounded elbow and knee joints. Use opaque diffuse materials only: metallic=0 and roughness=1 exactly. Provide idle, working, making_something and milestone_level_up authored clips through the ten body controls. Head, hands and dragon remain rest descendants without inferred finger/head control. A small golden craft sphere is a declared new action prop; no dynamic sculpting or physical simulation. Produce scene data for the weft-v1 output profile, not a replacement for Weft physics or its importer.
